chapter: Leaving St. Louis: Toby show, Darrell Harris and Eli Rice
title: Foiling Darrell Harris's getaway with the payroll
summary: The musicians, hosted by a kind white family, tipped off the club owner so Harris's payroll was garnisheed at the ballroom when he tried to collect his money and flee.

bands.name: Darrell Harris and his Black Diamond Orchestra

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Do you mean George Johnson was with you?

Oh, yeah, we were with the Black Diamond. George is a very fine musician, fine arranger, handsome cat. He went for the chicks, the chicks went for him. But, he'd sit down and play the music. So, ... Eli liked the idea of a trumpet and a saxophone player both rights. So we needed some money to bail ourselves out of the town and we owed some money there. In the meantime, I don't give a damn if this plugs or not, it's very important to me. This cat, Darrell Harris, had gone to, his boys had gotten together around 10:30 tonight he's going to pick up the money and split. In the meantime, I'm living here. We were living here. The little girl was sick ... and leave her with no money. Sometimes this is important. Now, a son-in-law had come up from a town right down from this one, Muskegon, Michigan. And he resented the fact that we were there Sunday, his family being there. So she told him now didn't like the fact that these folks are here, you can go home because these folks are my guests. So I got to, you know me. We don't want to disturb him. Still owe them money. Disturb the family. No, let him go. The daughter said, Let him go. So the guy stole the money. We haven't paid the woman/for this sleeping and eating. Very nice people. Split the scene. So the word got out so
at 10:30 at night, he's going to pick up the loot. So we had hipped the cat who owned the joint. And we had put, I don't know what you call those things, like you put a lock on ...
Oh, yeah, you kind of lock the thing up.

Yeah, you know, because this man's place, a helluva nice fellow. So he said, What? Had to go through 4 or 5 of us, I think it cost us $2.50 and we got it altogether so we can make it ... So he goes, the guy next to me says, he's going to make his move, 10:30 Saturday night. The bus driver is hollering because he wants his money. He's been driving, what the hell. He's going to leave everybody. So in the meantime as he goes, he's a leader so he goes to pick up the loot. The fellows up here His clothes are packed. He's splitting. He's got a car on the side. So he goes back, all dapper and that kind of thing. He says, Well, intermission is time to pick up the money. Mr. Harris, you have no money here. He says, Why? I don't remember the words, Stanley, he said because this money has been, you know?

Yeah, or something like that. And he walked back the most to the bandstand surprised person in the world. So I said, let's strike up the band. Let's play a little 'St. Louis Blues.' So, anyhow, to make a long story short, after that we Eli wanted $150. Oh, yeah, we got it. Seventy-five for George, seventy-five for me, which allowed us both to leave something for May and Willy so they could get home. We didn't (...?)
